additions.source_quote: וַהֲרִיחוֹ בְּיִרְאַת ה' וְכוּ' – זֶה בְּחִינַת חֹטֶם
additions.source_location: Torah #2, section א (paragraph 3 in source text), citing Isaiah 11:3
additions.reasoning: The verse 'וַהֲרִיחוֹ בְּיִרְאַת ה'' is cited as the proof that prayer = חֹטֶם: the nose of Mashiach smells and discerns via יִרְאַת ה'. The text says explicitly 'זֶה בְּחִינַת חֹטֶם.' This makes יִרְאַת ה' an aspect of חֹטֶם (= prayer), and it should be a bechina edge: יִרְאַת ה' <-> חֹטֶם, reference=2. Node would join Package 1.

additions.source_quote: בְּחַרְבִּי וּבְקַשְׁתִּי. וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י: תְּפִלָּה וּבַקָּשָׁה
additions.source_location: Torah #2, section א (paragraph 4 in source text), citing Genesis 48:22 with Rashi
additions.reasoning: Rashi's interpretation of 'בְּחַרְבִּי וּבְקַשְׁתִּי' = 'תְּפִלָּה וּבַקָּשָׁה' makes both חֶרֶב and קֶשֶׁת aspects of prayer. The dataset has the edge חֶרֶב <-> תְּפִלָּה (reference=2, bechina) but lacks the parallel edge קַשְׁתִּי <-> תְּפִלָּה. The source cites both weapons in one sentence — both are equally 'בְּחִינַת תְּפִלָּה.'

additions.source_quote: וְהַנְּשָׁמוֹת הַמְלֻבָּשִׁין בַּתְּפִלָּה הַמּוּבָאוֹת לַצַּדִּיק שֶׁבַּדּוֹר הֵם בִּבְחִינַת בְּתוּלוֹת אַחֲרֶיהָ רֵעוֹתֶיהָ מוּבָאוֹת לָךְ
additions.source_location: Torah #2, section ו (paragraph 23 in source text), citing Psalms 45:15
additions.reasoning: The souls garbed in prayer and brought to the Tzaddik are explicitly 'בִּבְחִינַת בְּתוּלוֹת אַחֲרֶיהָ.' This is an explicit bechina: souls-in-prayer ARE the virgins following the bride to the king. A missing edge: בְּתוּלוֹת <-> נְשָׁמוֹת (reference=2, bechina). Node belongs to Package 2.

additions.source_quote: וְהַתְּפִלָּה מְאִירָה לְהַנְּשָׁמוֹת בִּבְחִינַת חִדּוּשִׁין, שֶׁהִיא מְחַדֶּשֶׁת אוֹתָם בִּבְחִינַת עִבּוּר
additions.source_location: Torah #2, section ו (paragraph 22 in source text)
additions.reasoning: Prayer renews the souls 'בִּבְחִינַת עִבּוּר' (in the aspect of gestation/embryonic renewal). This is a bechina relationship: the renewal of souls in prayer IS the aspect of עִבּוּר (a fetus growing in the womb). The concept is mentioned twice (lines 20, 22). It belongs to Package 2 as an aspect of the soul-renewal process.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.context: Mashiach smells and discerns via fear of God — this IS the nose (חֹטֶם) = prayer. Source: וַהֲרִיחוֹ בְּיִרְאַת ה', זֶה בְּחִינַת חֹטֶם
Parallel weapon to חֶרֶב in Jacob's bequest — also = prayer per Rashi. Source: בְּחַרְבִּי וּבְקַשְׁתִּי = תְּפִלָּה וּבַקָּשָׁה. חֶרֶב is in dataset; קֶשֶׁת/קַשְׁתִּי is not.
Souls garbed in prayer brought to the Tzaddik ARE the virgins of Ps. 45. Source: הַנְּשָׁמוֹת הַמְלֻבָּשִׁין בַּתְּפִלָּה הֵם בִּבְחִינַת בְּתוּלוֹת אַחֲרֶיהָ רֵעוֹתֶיהָ
Prayer renews souls in the aspect of embryonic gestation. Source: שֶׁהִיא מְחַדֶּשֶׁת אוֹתָם בִּבְחִינַת עִבּוּר. Mentioned twice.

The state of divine hiding in exile — its two sides (face=rachamin, back=din) are in dataset, but the overarching concept הַסְתָּרַת פָּנִים as its own bechina node is not. Thematically belongs to Package 7.

classification_notes: All 44 bechina edges are accounted for and assigned to packages.
17 non-bechina (eitza) edges for Torah #2 were correctly excluded from package-building per the framework.

The bechina edge קלקול המשפט <-> קלקול לעינים at line 27102 is classified as 'eitza' in the dataset — this is correct per framework (corruption of mishpat CAUSES corruption of eyes). These nodes are linked by eitza, not bechina, and are placed in Package 6 based on their shared evil nature rather than a bechina bridge.

The dataset also contains a second occurrence of the קלקול המשפט <-> מחשבות רעות edge (id=null, reference=2) typed as 'eitza' — this represents the causal flow from mishpat-corruption to foreign thoughts, correctly typed.

Package 7 (חֶסֶד וְרַחֲמִים בְּגָלוּת) is marked 'neutral' because chesed, din, and rachamin are divine attributes that function as the structural framework of exile — they are not intrinsically good or evil but describe the divine posture in galut.

The edge מִשְׁפָּט <-> צְדָקָה at line 26266 is typed 'eitza' in the dataset — correct, as צְדָקָה LEADS TO מִשְׁפָּט (it is the mechanism for acquiring mishpat). Note however that the source also says they co-inhere ('מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה בְּיַעֲקֹב') — צְדָקָה might warrant inclusion in Package 3 as a bechina, but the dataset correctly treats the primary relationship as eitza.
